people.name: Joy Williams
people.description: Joy Williams American singer-songwriter who performed with John Paul White as The Civil Wars from 2009 until 2012 and scored the 2014 US No.1 album The Civil Wars.

people.name: Travis Barker
people.description: American musician, songwriter, and music producer Travis Barker who is the drummer for the rock band Blink-182. They had the 2000 UK No.2 single 'All The Small Things' and the 2001 US No.1 album Take Off Your.... Due to his fame, Rolling Stone referred to him as "punk's first superstar drummer", as well as one of the 100 greatest drummers of all time.

people.name: Faye Tozer
people.description: Faye Tozer, singer with British dance-pop group Steps. Between 1997 and 2001, Steps scored two No.1 singles in the UK, two No.1 albums and 14 consecutive UK top 5 singles. In addition to earning a BRIT Award nomination in 1999, for Best Newcomer, the group would be an opening support act for Britney Spears on her debut American tour the same year.

people.name: Andrew Strong
people.description: Irish singer Andrew Strong. He starred as Deco Cuffe in the 1991 cult film The Commitments based on the book by Roddy Doyle, despite being only 17 at the time of its release.

people.name: Douglas Payne
people.description: Douglas Payne, bassist with Scottish rock band Travis. Their 1999 UK album The Man Who spent nine weeks at No.1 on the UK Charts and one-hundred and thirty-four weeks in the top 100 of the chart. Travis had and 1999 UK No.10 single 'Why Does It Always Rain On Me', plus over 10 other UK Top 40 singles.

people.name: Brendan Benson
people.description: American musician and singer-songwriter Brendan Benson. He has released seven solo albums and is a member of the band The Raconteurs with Jack White.

people.name: Adina Howard
people.description: American singer and songwriter Adina Howard. She rose to fame during the mid-1990s with her debut album, Do You Wanna Ride? and her debut single, 'Freak like Me', and the 1996 UK No.2 single with Warren G, 'What's Love Got To Do With It'.

people.name: Butch Walker
people.description: American singer-songwriter and record producer Butch Walker. He was lead guitarist for the glam metal band, South Gang and became the lead vocalist for the rock band, Marvelous 3. Walker has worked with many artists, including, Pink, Green Day, Taylor Swift, Ed Sheeran and Frank Turner.

people.name: Brian Yale
people.description: Brian Yale, Matchbox Twenty who rose to international fame with their debut album, Yourself or Someone Like You (1996), which was certified 12× Platinum in the United States and multi-platinum in Australia, Canada and New Zealand.

people.name: Nina Gordon
people.description: American singer, songwriter, and guitarist Nina Gordon. She co-founded the alternative rock band Veruca Salt and played on their first two studio albums, American Thighs (1994) and Eight Arms to Hold You (1997).

people.name: Joseph Simmons
people.description: Joseph 'Run' Simmons, one of the founding members of the influential hip hop group Run–D.M.C. who had the 1986 UK No.8 single with Aerosmith 'Walk This Way' and the 1998 UK No.1 single 'It's Like That'. He is also a practicing minister, known as Reverend Run.

people.name: Andrew Banfield
people.description: British singer Andrew Banfield from English R&B/pop group Pasadenas, who had the 1992 UK No.4 single 'I'm Doing Fine Now'.

people.name: Drew Zingg
people.description: American rock, blues, soul and jazz guitarist Drew Zingg. He toured and recorded with Steely Dan, Boz Scaggs, Michael McDonald, and Phoebe Snow, among others. Zingg died in San Francisco on 7 April 2025, at the age of 67.

people.name: Alec John Such
people.description: Alec John Such, bass, Bon Jovi, (1987 US No.1 & UK No.4 single 'Livin' On A Prayer', 1986 US No.1 album 'Slippery When Wet' has sold over 8 million copies world wide). He died on 4 June 2022 age 70.

people.name: Frankie Banali
people.description: American rock drummer Frankie Banali. He is most widely known for his work with multi-platinum heavy metal band Quiet Riot and also worked with W.A.S.P. and Billy Idol. He died om 20 Aug 2020 from pancreatic cancer age 68.

people.name: Steven Bishop
people.description: American singer-songwriter, actor, and guitarist Steven Bishop. He had the 1976 album Careless and sang the theme for the film Tootsie, and scored the 1977 US No.11 single 'On And On'. He has also written many different songs for other artists, such as Barbra Streisand, Phil Collins and Art Garfunkel.

people.name: Leo van de Ketterij
people.description: Dutch guitarist Leo van de Ketterij, from the Dutch rock band Shocking Blue, who formed in The Hague in 1967. They had the 1970 US No.1 & UK No.8 single 'Venus' which topped the charts in nine countries and was the first song by a Dutch band to reach No. 1 on the US chart. Worldwide, the single has sold over 5 million copies. Bananarama covered 'Venus' in 1986, hitting No.1 in the United States, Canada, and Australia, and reaching No.8 in the UK. American rock band Nirvana recorded a cover version of the Shocking Blue song 'Love Buzz' for its 1988 debut single, released on Sub Pop in the USA. He died on 5 July 2021.

people.name: James Young
people.description: American musician James Young who is best known as one of the guitarists and occasional lead vocalists in the American rock band Styx, who had the 1979 US No.1 & 1980 UK No.6 single 'Babe'.

people.name: Cornell Gunter
people.description: Cornell Gunter, who was an original member of The Platters. He later joined The Coasters who scored the 1958 US No.1 single 'Yakety Yak', the 1959 US No.2 and UK No.6 single 'Charlie Brown', as well as 'Young Blood' and 'Poison Ivy'. Gunter was murdered in Las Vegas, Nevada, after being shot in his car on 26th February 1990.

people.name: Joe Billingslea
people.description: American singer Joe Billingslea the lead singer and founder of the R&B band The Contours, best known for their 1962 hit single, 'Do You Love Me', (written by Motown Records founder Berry Gordy Jr.).

people.name: Freddie Garrity
people.description: Freddie Garrity, singer and actor who was the frontman and comical element in the 1960s pop band Freddie and the Dreamers. They scored the 1963 UK No.3 single 'You Were made For Me', and the 1965 US No.1 single 'I'm Telling You Now'. Garrity died on 19th May 2006 aged 69.

works.title: In the Court of the Crimson King
works.eventDescription: English poet and songwriter Pete Sinfield died at the age of 80. He was best known as a co-founder and lyricist of King Crimson. Their debut album In the Court of the Crimson King is considered one of the first and most influential progressive rock albums ever released. He later wrote a number of successful songs for artists such as Celine Dion, Cher, Cliff Richard, Leo Sayer, Five Star, and Bucks Fizz.

works.title: (If Paradise Is) Half as Nice
works.eventDescription: Welsh drummer Dennis Bryon died in Nashville at the age of 75. With Amen Corner he had the 1969 UK No.1 single 'If Paradise Is Half As Nice', plus five other UK Top 40 hits. He also worked with The Bee Gees, playing drums on all recordings, television, and tours from 1973 to 1980, including nine No.1 singles.

works.title: Disco
works.eventDescription: Kylie Minogue was at No.1 with her fifteenth studio album Disco. The album was later nominated in categories at the 2021 Billboard Music Awards and 2021 ARIA Music Awards.

works.title: If I Can Dream
works.eventDescription: A pair of white boots worn by Elvis Presley during his famous '68 Comeback TV Special performance were bought by a UK collector for £29,500, ($44,500). Elvis had worn the size-11 Verde boots while singing 'If I Can Dream', two months after the assassination of Martin Luther King, the lyrics included quotes from the civil rights leader.

works.title: Forty Licks
works.eventDescription: The Rolling Stones were refused permission to pursue a claim against their former record company Decca for unpaid royalties through the courts. A High Court judge in London said the dispute would go to arbitration and not be decided in court. The dispute was over their Forty Licks compilation CD, which was released in 2002 and was the first collection to span their entire career.

works.title: Vertigo
works.eventDescription: U2 went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Vertigo', the bands fifth UK No.1, taken from 'How To Dismantle An Atomic Bomb'.

works.title: China in Your Hand
works.eventDescription: T'Pau started a five week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'China In Your Hand'. The song's title according to singer Carol Decker is the effect you get if you hold a china cup to a light, you can see your hand through it.

works.title: Faith
works.eventDescription: George Michael went to No.1 on the UK album chart with his debut solo album 'Faith'. The album won several awards including the Grammy Award for Album of the Year in 1989. To date, the album has sold over 20 million copies worldwide. Between 1987 and 1988, Faith produced six Top 5 Billboard Hot 100 hits, four of which ('Faith', 'Father Figure', 'One More Try', and 'Monkey') reached No.1, making him the only British male singer to have four No.1 singles from one LP on the Billboard Hot 100.

works.title: Sugar Sugar
works.eventDescription: 'Sugar Sugar' by The Archies was at No.1 on the UK singles chart. The single became the longest running One Hit Wonder in the UK with eight week's at the top of the charts. It was the first No.1 performed by cartoon characters.

works.title: Georgia on My Mind
works.eventDescription: Ray Charles went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Georgia On My Mind', a No.24 hit in the UK. His cover of Hoagy Carmichael's 1930 standard, became the first of three No.1 hits for the singer. In 1979, the State of Georgia designated Ray Charles' version the official state song and the song has become part of the Great American Songbook tradition.
